public_rationale: Read plainly, 'It didn't' means that by December 2025, scaling LLMs had not produced general intelligence. Leading scaling proponents said as much. In August 2025 Sam Altman said GPT-5 was still 'missing something quite important' compared with AGI as most people define it. In November 2025 Ilya Sutskever said he did not think 100x more scale would transform everything, and that the field was 'back to the age of research'. Google DeepMind's Oriol Vinyals said pre-training scaling still gave big gains, but he did not claim AGI. So scaling kept improving models without reaching AGI. Only the past-tense part is graded, not the 'never'.
limitations: Rests on reading 'work' as 'reach AGI'. Scaling clearly did produce large capability gains.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling large language models did not work as a path to general intelligence.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that scaled LLMs had reached generally recognised AGI by the post date, or that scaling alone was broadly shown to be on track to produce it.
